prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and for the experimental observation of helical edge-channel transport in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep a single-part prize for the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, credited to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After reading the whole first round and the chair's summary, my judgement of the science is unchanged. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant insulators with spin-orbit coupling fall into distinct classes labelled by a Z2 invariant, and that this has a measurable consequence, namely protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group observed exactly that edge transport in HgTe/CdTe wells. The interpretation has been stable for more than fifteen years across many materials, so I do not see a maturity problem in the science. The chair records that three members back this trio and that the other leading groups call it a respectable alternative. I treat that as agreement about the physics, not as a substitute for it. The only open questions are the wording of the citation and the edges of the credit, and I think both can be handled by a narrow citation.
statement.case_against: The credit is still not complete. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp tested and Zhang cannot be recognised. Hasan, Fu and Moore carried the idea to three dimensions, which a three-name cap leaves out. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases of matter is adjacent, so the citation must show what is new here. I also accept that B010 has the cleanest two-name credit on the shortlist and the broadest independent confirmation of a measured result. If the committee judges the B047 allocation unsettled, B010 is a better fallback than a wider or looser topological prize.

responses.point: Kroll weighs the step change in measurement capability for optical lattice clocks, near 1e-18 uncertainty, and the cleanest credit boundary on the shortlist, and the chair asks whether Mehlig and others accept the magic-wavelength distinction from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I accept part of this. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea from the comb and from ion control, because it lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once without a trap-induced shift. That answers my continuity worry as a matter of the scheme's logic, so I no longer argue that B010 is already honoured. What I still weigh differently is the kind of result. A lattice clock is a decisive instrument, whereas the Z2 classification changed how insulators are organised. This is a difference in kind and in weight, not a flaw in the pair, and I would not block B010. I keep it as my first alternative and I have moved it above B051 for that reason.

responses.point: Danielsson would credit Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, and in round 1 said he would not oppose B047 if the attribution can be settled; he also prefers B051 and calls it a prediction followed by observation.
responses.response: I still disagree with dropping Mele. The Z2 invariant and the graphene quantum spin Hall proposal come from the joint Kane-Mele papers, so removing him cuts the theoretical core to make room for the three-dimensional chapter. Hasan's ARPES experiments depend on the Fu-Kane-Mele theory and belong to a later step. On B051, I agree the 2011 prediction and 2018 observation form a real chain. My difference is maturity of interpretation, since the pairing mechanism is unsettled and Cao is outside any three names. The B047 case is complete on both sides, and the same cannot be said yet for B051, so I keep B051 as my second alternative.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers Mele to Hasan as the origin of the Z2 invariant, shares the 2016 overlap concern, and keeps B051 as an alternative.
responses.response: We agree on the trio. On the 2016 overlap, my answer is that the 2016 prize rests on Chern-type invariants and integer quantum Hall phases, which need no time-reversal symmetry and have chiral edge states. The Z2 insulator is a time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-driven phase with helical edges, and it was observed in a different system. I think a citation that names the Z2 invariant and helical edge transport answers the overlap, and I would accept your wording on it. I take your point that the credit is defensible but not exhaustive and I would record that in the citation rather than add names.

responses.point: Johansson names B046 as his first alternative if the B047 allocation cannot be settled, and he would recuse from circuit QED.
responses.response: I think the allocation can be settled with the 2D prediction-and-observation chain and a narrow citation, so I would not move to B046. B046 had support from only three members in the opening round, and it concerns theory proposals whose experimental weight is spread over many groups. I note that your disclosure on circuit QED removes B041 from your vote, and I agree that it is a poor choice this year given the 2025 prize.

responses.point: Olsson cites the 2016 prize as a risk for B047 and raises whether to wait for the redefinition of the second before awarding B010.
responses.response: On 2016, I hope the answer to Eriksson above also addresses your concern. On waiting for the redefinition, I do not think it should decide anything. The science of lattice clocks does not depend on it, and it would be a reason to delay B010 only if the committee wanted a result that is already formalised. I do not hold that against Katori and Ye.

uncertainties: Whether the three-name cap is fair to Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and to Hasan, Fu and Moore, or whether the citation wording alone can carry the acknowledgement.
Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough room for a separate Z2 prize, which depends on how narrowly the citation is worded.
Whether a prize that honours a conceptual classification should rank above a decisive measurement capability such as B010. I regard this as a judgement of kind, not a fact the evidence can settle.
statement.conflict_note: I still have no specific conflict apparent from my profile. My work on statistical physics, turbulence and neural networks does not overlap with topological insulators or lattice clocks, and I have no documented connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori or Ye. I have no basis for recusal on any part.
